- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above immediate prior high.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., >0.30 for 3+ days), model frequently overreacts; apply downward bias of 1–3% to prevent overcorrection.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is weak or neutral (e.g., sentiment < -0.20 for 5+ days); add 1–3% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-cycle mean reversion; adjust final 5–7 days downward if sentiment turns negative or stabilizes.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; add 1–2% to forecast for early-cycle bullish sentiment.
- When sentiment is volatile (±0.30 or more), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before final output.
